summary: Repeated event forecasting requires extracting predictive signals from noisy evidence and evaluating their value across successive decisions. We introduce JockeyBench, a benchmark and evaluation protocol that studies this problem through historical Japanese horse racing.
takeaways: The protocol combines time-gated evidence, priced tools, paired frozen-program controls, and two workflows: executing an LLM-written predictor or acquiring evidence for a fresh per-race LLM forecast.
Evaluation separates forecast quality, benchmark-specific net utility, and retrospective betting returns and risk under fixed decision rules.
In a four-model comparison, the reusable-program workflow has higher mean betting profit and lower research fees, although both workflows lose on average.
